requirement: Apply for a Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) to use the State land / property
why: SLA rents State land and properties for short-term uses (events up to 90 days) through TOLs; without the land owner's consent the other permits have no venue to attach to.
note: SLA's page gives no processing time — ask SLA early.

requirement: Get a Town Council permit to use the void deck / open space
why: Void decks and open spaces in HDB estates are common property managed by the Town Council, which issues the booking permit.
note: Checked for Bishan-Toa Payoh TC only (bookings open up to 6 months ahead, residents only, variety shows not permitted at void decks). Other Town Councils differ.

requirement: Get NParks approval to use park premises for the event
why: Parks are managed by NParks; using park premises for an event needs its approval. Nature parks and the Rail Corridor also need a group activity permit (>30 people) at least 1 month ahead.
note: GoBusiness page blocked our tool; group-permit lead time verified on NParks' own page (src-nparks-ogap).

requirement: Confirm who controls the street and how to use road or walkway space
why: Streets and five-foot ways must stay passable; using them for an event needs the road authority's agreement. We did not find the official page in time.

requirement: Identify who owns or manages the site before planning anything else
why: Every other permit needs the site owner's consent first; the owner of this site is not confirmed.

requirement: Check whether the performance is exempt from licensing; if not, apply for an Arts Entertainment Licence
why: Public arts performances need an Arts Entertainment Licence unless they meet an exemption's conditions. IMDA asks for applications at least 40 working days before the event (about 8–9 weeks once public holidays are counted).
note: Exemption conditions: see src-spf-exempt. Ordering after venue consent is our assumption.

requirement: If relying on an exemption that requires it, notify the Police at least 7 days before
why: Some licence-exempt entertainment is exempt only if the organiser notifies the Police at least 7 days ahead and keeps to the listed conditions (hours, loudspeakers, set-up times).

requirement: Check whether the stage, tent or installation frame needs a temporary-structure or fire-safety approval
why: Temporary structures that the public stands on or under can need structural and fire-safety checks. We did not open the official pages in time.

requirement: Check food licensing for the pop-up stall
why: Selling or giving out food at a public event usually needs a temporary food licence; some Town Councils also restrict cooking at void decks.

requirement: Agree sound levels, speaker placement and finishing time with the venue manager
why: Amplified sound near homes is the most common cause of complaints; exemption conditions also limit loudspeakers and hours.

requirement: Declare that the event is ticketed and check how fees and conditions change
why: Charging admission makes the event commercial, which can change venue fees and rules out some funding (e.g. the Lively Places Fund does not support commercial events).
